title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Throughout, Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Its extension Π̂_{0,3}^∼ = Π̂_{0,3}·{1,τ_0} adjoins a 'real' involution τ_0, and it carries the S_3 symmetry of the three punctures, generated by an order-3 element ρ and an involution σ_∞. The l_i are inertia generators and L_0 is the inertia subgroup at 0. φ̂ is a fixed comparison map (from the 'équation des lacets' set-up) that is equivariant up to inner automorphisms. M^{!∼}_{0,3} is a group of 'lacet' automorphisms.

Previous page. Grothendieck showed that automorphisms u commuting externally with φ̂ correspond bijectively to pairs (ξ,f). Only ξ is constrained:
- (14) ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1, a 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation;
- (15) ξ = φ̂(ξ) σ_∞(φ̂(ξ))^{-1} l_1^ν, a 2-cycle relation, with 2ν+1 a unit in Ẑ.
The automorphism is recovered by (17): u(σ_∞) = int(f^{-1})(ξ l_1^{-ν} σ_∞) and u(ρ) = int(f^{-1})(ξ ρ).

This page. He normalises by taking f = 1 and names u_ξ the automorphism attached to the pair (ξ,1). So:
- (18) u_ξ(σ_∞) = ξ l_1^{-ν} σ_∞ and u_ξ(ρ) = ξ ρ.
- (19) The general element is then u_{ξ,f} = int(f^{-1}) ∘ u_ξ. The f-dependence is purely inner, so modulo inner automorphisms everything depends on ξ alone.
- (20) Formulas (5),(6) give the strict, not merely external, commutation φ̂ ∘ u_ξ = u_ξ ∘ φ̂ (on the left, u_ξ is restricted to Π̂_{0,3}).

Corollary 3. The (ξ-normalised, in the sense of p.416) automorphisms of Π̂^{∼}_{0,3} of the form u_ξ are exactly those that commute strictly with φ̂ and normalise the inertia subgroup L_0.

Next page. The converse check: normalising L_0 forces f = l_0^n, and strict commutation forces φ̂(f) = f, hence n = 0. This yields Corollary 4: the u_ξ form a subgroup M^{!≈}_{0,3}(ω) of the normaliser of L_0. It meets the inner automorphisms trivially and maps isomorphically onto the externally defined group N^{!≈}_{0,3}.

What it serves. This is a rigidification (canonical section) of an outer-automorphism group of the tower of profinite fundamental groups of the M_{0,n}. A normalised automorphism is pinned down by a single 'cocycle' ξ satisfying 2- and 3-cycle relations. This is the mechanism by which Drinfeld/Ihara's GT is defined from pairs (λ,f) with f normalised so that it lies in the derived subgroup, which kills the inner ambiguity.
errors: The machine transcription of (18) gives (ξ l_1^{-ν})^2 σ_∞. By consistency with (17) at f=1 the formula should read u_ξ(σ_∞) = ξ l_1^{-ν} σ_∞. The mark above the bracket is most likely an annotation (ν or an overbrace), not an exponent. Otherwise no mathematical errors are visible.
Corollary 3 is stated without proof on this page; the verification is supplied on the next page.

ideas.what: Parametrising φ̂-compatible automorphisms of the S_3-extended profinite π_1(P^1 − 3 points) by an element ξ satisfying a 3-cycle relation (14) and a 2-cycle relation (15) involving an exponent ν with 2ν+1 a unit (by analogy with GT, the parameter λ would correspond to 2ν+1)
ideas.modern_name: Pentagon/hexagon-type defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT (pairs (λ,f))
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches GT via the 'lego' of M_{0,3}, M_{0,4}; this explicit computation is in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation

ideas.what: Normalising the automorphism (f=1) so that the inner-automorphism ambiguity disappears, giving a section of Aut → Out (u_{ξ,f} = int(f^{-1}) u_ξ)
ideas.modern_name: Normalised GT elements / f in the derived subgroup; lifting outer actions to genuine automorphisms

ideas.what: Characterisation of the normalised automorphisms as those commuting strictly with φ̂ and normalising the inertia subgroup L_0

missed.claim: Grothendieck has an explicit derivation of a GT-like group as the φ̂-commuting, L_0-normalising automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3}^∼. Each is determined by a unique ξ subject to a 3-cycle and a 2-cycle relation (with an exponent ν, 2ν+1 a unit), and the group is isomorphic to its outer image (Cor. 3–4). This predates Drinfeld's definition of GT.
missed.quote: Corollaire 3 Les automorphismes (ξ-normalisés) ... de la forme u_ξ sont exactement ceux pour lesquels on a les formules (20) (i.e. qui commutent à φ̂) et qui de plus normalisent L_0.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents Grothendieck's own route to the GT relations, through the S_3-extended group and inertia normalisation, as distinct from Drinfeld's quasi-Hopf route. Historians of GT and specialists comparing variants (GT, \hat{GT} with complex conjugation, inertia-preserving automorphism groups) may find the precise formulation, including the real involution τ_0, of interest.

deep.surprise_reason: It is known in outline from the Esquisse that Grothendieck anticipated GT. This page gives a concrete, careful normalisation and characterisation result in his own formalism, which is a notable but not shocking unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: (18): u_ξ(σ_∞) = (ξ l_1^{-ν}) σ_∞; the '2'/'ν' above is an overbrace annotation, not a square.
'Faisons[?]' is probably 'Désignons [par] ... ((14)(15))', i.e. it refers to formulas (14),(15), not (4).
'u_ξ ↾ 2-ν[?]' in Corollary 3 likely reads 'u_ξ' followed by the superscripted note '(ξ normalisés*)'; the group is Π̂^{∼}_{0,3}.
'dans le premier membre[?]' fits the image and the sense (left-hand side of (20)).
